question.text: 'Mahanadi PE Fund II', a close-ended Category II AIF, is approaching the end of its initial 7-year tenure. The Manager seeks to extend tenure. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the permissible extension framework?

answer.text: Extension up to 2 years, subject to approval of two-thirds of unit holders by value of their investment
Extension up to 5 years with simple majority of unit holders
Unlimited extensions are permitted as long as the Manager discloses in PPM
No extension permitted; fund must liquidate on the original maturity date

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 13(4): Extension of tenure of close-ended Cat I and Cat II AIFs is permitted up to 2 years, subject to approval of two-thirds of unit holders by value. In absence of consent, the AIF must fully liquidate within one year following expiration of the (extended or original) tenure. The Trap: Option B confuses with AI-only Fund 5-year extension. Option C is wrong — hard ceiling of 2 years. Option D ignores the 2-year extension window. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests tenure-extension votes. XIX-C adds the LVF and AI-only-Fund differential (AI-only Funds can extend up to 5 years with two-thirds consent). Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Start LP-advisory-committee outreach for tenure extension 9-12 months before expiry. Tie the extension to a revised management-fee step-down schedule to get LP consent — a common market practice. Document the 2/3 consent in writing with value-weighted votes; simple majority by head count is NOT sufficient.
